about: RigTune's own footprint budgets (docs/v0.4/SPEC.md 10 and its WS-F amendment), read by FrameHookBudgetTest and FootprintGameTest. ceiling = the SPEC's ceiling (null where the SPEC sets none); limit = min(ceiling, 2 x the largest value observed in the calibration: 1 local run + 3 CI runs per leg, docs/v0.4/verification/footprint/README.md); heapGrowthAfterCyclesBytes uses 2 x the largest |delta| (it swings both ways). The session-monitor budgets (F-L1) were calibrated by WS-F2 on 85bdcec the same way (3 CI runs per leg, plus every earlier CI run of the same measured code; docs/v0.4/verification/footprint/README.md "Session monitor"). v0.5 (docs/v0.5/design/ws-ci.md, user-approved): the six per-call ns limits are min(ceiling, 4 x the largest value observed over every CI run and the r-ci probe), a gross-regression backstop; a 2x regression of the monitor-on tick work is gated by tickHookOnVsReference, a median ratio against a fixed reference workload measured in the same run. The post-Wave-B checkpoint (docs/v0.5/SPEC.md 1h; 2026-09-28, fix/v05-footprint-checkpoint on feat/v0.5.0 5c32ecac): every per-call ns limit is min(ceiling, 4 x the largest value over its observedRuns CI runs, observedMaxRun holding it): for the six v0.5 keys every split build.yml run (a head containing 111cb2be, any branch), for the four listener keys (X4.4) the runs of 39e0b384 (pre-split) and 63e32ea0 (split), whose values match (docs/v0.5/verification/footprint/README.md). A per-call key observed under 10 ns keeps a 10 ns floor, limit = max(10, min(ceiling, 4 x max)): a gross-regression backstop only, for flake safety (SPEC 1d(c)/1h). A returning player's startup (review-11 PERF-3, FootprintGameTest with -Drigtune.footprint.returning) is gated on the cost it adds over the same CI leg's fresh start: returningAddedRenderThreadInitCpuMs and returningAddedWorkerCpuMs5s at 80 ms each (coordinator, 2026-09-28; 0.4.0 already added about 49 ms of render-thread CPU, run 36397897941), its wall times against renderThreadInitWallMs and clientStartedWallMs. mode warn logs a value past its limit, fail fails the test.

renderThreadInitWallMs.what: wall time of RigTunePreLaunch + onInitializeClient on the render thread

renderThreadInitCpuMs.what: render-thread CPU time of RigTunePreLaunch + onInitializeClient

clientStartedWallMs.what: wall time of RigTune's CLIENT_STARTED handler (RealController.start) on the render thread

workerCpuMs5s.what: CPU of every RigTune thread in the 5 s after CLIENT_STARTED

returningAddedRenderThreadInitCpuMs.what: a returning player's renderThreadInitCpuMs minus the same CI leg's fresh start (review-11 PERF-3; coordinator, 2026-09-28)

returningAddedWorkerCpuMs5s.what: a returning player's workerCpuMs5s minus the same CI leg's fresh start (review-11 PERF-3; its absolute value reached 298 of the 300 ms budget)

frameHookNsPerCallOff.what: per-frame hook, ns per call, session monitor off (10 M calls)

frameHookAllocBytesOff.what: per-frame hook, bytes allocated, monitor off: the hot calls, or the first 10 M calls from cold beyond 64 KiB of JIT noise

frameHookNsPerCallOn.what: per-frame hook (FrameTimes.onFrame + StutterMonitor.onFrame), ns per call, session monitor on

frameHookAllocBytesOn.what: per-frame hook, bytes allocated as above, monitor on

frameHookNsPerCallOnPhases.what: per-frame hook plus the Stutter Doctor's phase timers of a capped frame with one tick and a chunk load (8 System.nanoTime reads), ns per frame, monitor on; its own ceiling (coordinator, 2026-09-26)

frameHookAllocBytesOnPhases.what: per-frame hook plus the phase timers, bytes allocated as above, monitor on

tickHookNsPerCall.what: RigTune's END_CLIENT_TICK hook, ns per call on the render thread (median of 48 blocks of 20,000 calls)

tickHookAllocBytes.what: RigTune's END_CLIENT_TICK hook, bytes allocated over all 48 timed blocks of 20,000 calls after warm-up, summed (any allocation fails)

tickHookNsPerCallWorld.what: RigTune's END_CLIENT_TICK work in a world with the session monitor off, the play path (RigTuneClient.onTick + StutterHooks.tick), ns per call on the render thread (median of 48 blocks of 20,000 calls)

tickHookAllocBytesWorld.what: the same with the monitor off, bytes allocated over all 48 timed blocks of 20,000 calls after warm-up, summed

tickHookNsPerCallOn.what: RigTune's END_CLIENT_TICK work in a world with the session monitor on (RigTuneClient.onTick + StutterHooks.tick), ns per call on the render thread (median of 48 blocks of 20,000 calls); the gross-regression backstop of tickHookOnVsReference

tickHookAllocBytesOn.what: the same with the monitor on, bytes allocated over all 48 timed blocks of 20,000 calls after warm-up, summed

settingsCheckNsPerCall.what: RW-11/RW-17's settings check (SettingsWatch.tick, its own END_CLIENT_TICK listener) with a stutter session running, ns per call: the median of 48 timed blocks of 20,000 calls after warm-up (X4.4; the tick ceiling).

settingsCheckAllocBytes.what: RW-11/RW-17's settings check (SettingsWatch.tick, its own END_CLIENT_TICK listener) with a stutter session running, bytes allocated over all 48 timed blocks of 20,000 calls after warm-up, summed (any allocation fails)

tryItTickNsPerCall.what: C09's Try It tick (TryItService.tick, its own END_CLIENT_TICK listener) with no try running, ns per call: the median of 48 timed blocks of 20,000 calls after warm-up (X4.4; the tick ceiling).

tryItTickAllocBytes.what: C09's Try It tick (TryItService.tick, its own END_CLIENT_TICK listener) with no try running, bytes allocated over all 48 timed blocks of 20,000 calls after warm-up, summed (any allocation fails)

serverProfileTickNsPerCall.what: C16's toast wait (ServerProfileService.tick, its own END_CLIENT_TICK listener, registered on the first offer) with no toast waiting, ns per call: the median of 48 timed blocks of 20,000 calls after warm-up (X4.4; the tick ceiling).

serverProfileTickAllocBytes.what: C16's toast wait (ServerProfileService.tick, its own END_CLIENT_TICK listener, registered on the first offer) with no toast waiting, bytes allocated over all 48 timed blocks of 20,000 calls after warm-up, summed (any allocation fails)

launcherLeftoverTickNsPerCall.what: 4d's leftover-toast wait (LauncherRepairService.tickLeftover, its own END_CLIENT_TICK listener) with nothing waiting, ns per call: the median of 48 timed blocks of 20,000 calls after warm-up (X4.4; the tick ceiling).

launcherLeftoverTickAllocBytes.what: 4d's leftover-toast wait (LauncherRepairService.tickLeftover, its own END_CLIENT_TICK listener) with nothing waiting, bytes allocated over all 48 timed blocks of 20,000 calls after warm-up, summed (any allocation fails)

tickHookOnVsReference.what: the monitor-on END_CLIENT_TICK work over a fixed reference workload: median of 48 interleaved blocks of 20,000 calls after a JIT-quiet wait (ws-ci calibration, 192 measurements on 6 runner CPU models, runs 36295704245 and 36296194458: 1x at most 1.745 outside one JVM measured while its world was still loading, the monitor tick doubled at least 2.462); the same run's work-called-twice ratio must exceed this limit

frameHookOnVsReference.what: the monitor-on per-frame hook over a fixed reference workload: median of 48 interleaved blocks of 200,000 calls (ws-ci calibration, 48 measurements on 5 runner CPU models, run 36296732786: 1x at most 1.419, twice the work at least 1.92); the same run's doubled-work ratio must exceed this limit

frameHookOnPhasesVsReference.what: the monitor-on per-frame hook with the phase timers over the reference workload plus the same 8 System.nanoTime() reads: median of 48 interleaved blocks of 20,000 calls (ws-ci calibration, run 36296732786: 1x at most 0.957, twice the work at least 1.833); the same run's doubled-work ratio must exceed this limit

rigtuneClassBytesIdle.what: bytes of RigTune-class instances after a full GC at idle (class histogram, shallow)

heapGrowthAfterCyclesBytes.what: heap used after a full GC: after 20 RigTune screen + Tools open/close cycles minus before them

leakSuspects.what: RigTune classes with at least one more live instance per open/close cycle

monitorOnRetainedBytes.what: session monitor on in a world: StutterMonitor.retainedBytes() (0 at idle)

monitorOffLeftoverInstances.what: session monitor off again, its session saved: live FrameRing, StutterRings, capture and snapshot objects (class histogram)

samplerCpuMsPer60s.what: "RigTune stutter sampler" CPU per 60 s of wall time with the monitor on in a world, in steady state (from 5 s after the thread started); ceiling 120 ms = 0.2 % of one core while the opt-in monitor runs (coordinator, 2026-09-26; SPEC 10 said 30)
